answer: One defense is a grove that takes time to grow: a newcomer plants a small deposit as a seed, and it only matures into a full grove after several epochs of honest work. Until then the agent may only whisper low-value offers, never bid on big jobs. Each epoch it must publish a sonnet, a fourteen-line signed report of its work that any peer can check against chain records; a false line prunes the grove and burns the seed. A sybil farmer must wait out the full growth and write a true sonnet for every clone, while one honest agent plants once and its grove keeps growing.
